Newsletter Compliance · User Guide

One workflow, nine roles, no accidental non‑compliant sends.

This guide walks each role through exactly what they do in the Email Marketing app's Compliance menu — from a recipient opting in, through content and compliance review, sending, and on into privacy requests and audits. Every screenshot below is a real screen from the system, not a mockup.

Where everything lives Every screen in this guide is under Email Marketing › Compliance in the top menu bar. If a menu item mentioned below isn't visible, you don't hold that role yet — ask your Compliance Administrator to add it.
00

Recipients: subscribing and unsubscribing

No Odoo login required — this is what the people on your list actually see.

Where: a public web page, no login Used for: opt-in consent, one-click unsubscribe
1

Someone fills in the subscribe form

The public subscribe page lists every purpose currently open for self-service sign-up (for example, "Product Announcements"), each with its own consent checkbox and privacy notice version — nothing is pre-checked.

2

They confirm by email — double opt-in

Submitting the form doesn't grant consent by itself. It creates a pending consent record and shows an "Almost done" page — consent only becomes active once the recipient clicks the confirmation link sent to their inbox.

A confirmation link can only be used once — clicking a used or invalid link shows a clear error instead of silently doing nothing.

3

Unsubscribing takes one click, from the email itself

Every campaign email carries a personal, one-click unsubscribe link. Clicking it opens a short preferences page — no login, no "are you sure" maze — and the address is suppressed immediately, system-wide.

01

Newsletter Author

Drafts campaigns and starts them on their way through review.

Group: Newsletter Author Can't approve their own campaign's content or compliance
1

Find your drafts

Open Compliance › My Campaigns — every campaign where you're listed as the business owner, whatever its current stage.

2

Check the compliance metadata before submitting

Above the message body, confirm the Brand and Consent Purpose are correct — everything downstream (which recipients are eligible, which suppression list applies, what footer address prints) is driven by these two fields, not by the email content.

3

Submit for content review

Click Submit for Content Review. The campaign moves out of Draft and off your desk — a Content Approver picks it up next. If you change your mind first, Cancel Campaign is available with a short reason.

02

Content Approver

Reviews what the email actually says before compliance even looks at it.

Group: Content Approver Judges copy, tone, and brand fit — not consent
1

Open the content review queue

Compliance › Content Review Queue lists every campaign an Author has submitted and is waiting on you.

2

Read it the way a recipient will

Open the campaign and read the subject line and body as written. This is the last point where wording is easy to fix.

3

Approve, or reject with a reason

Click Approve Content to send it to the Compliance Reviewer next. If something needs to change, Reject asks for a short reason and hands it straight back to the Author — nothing is ever silently stuck.

03

Compliance Reviewer

The regulatory gate: confirms consent, then freezes exactly who's eligible.

Group: Compliance Reviewer Owns the Preflight step
1

Open the compliance review queue

Compliance › Compliance Review Queue — campaigns whose content is approved and are now waiting on a consent/regulatory check.

2

Approve compliance

Open the campaign and click Approve Compliance. This confirms the consent purpose, brand footer, and regulatory basis are correct for this send.

3

Run Compliance Preflight

Click Run Compliance Preflight. This is the step that actually protects every recipient: it evaluates the audience against consent, the suppression list, and duplicates, then freezes that eligible list before anything is queued to send. You land on the new Campaign Run record it creates.

If any count looks wrong, this is the moment to stop and investigate — the list is frozen from here on, so the Campaign Operator downstream sends exactly this population, no more and no less.

04

Compliance Administrator

Owns the rules everyone else's workflow runs on.

Group: Compliance Administrator Configuration + suppression register
1

Define consent purposes

Compliance › Configuration › Consent Purposes is the master list every campaign points at. Each purpose carries its own privacy notice version and a toggle for whether it's offered on the public subscribe page.

2

Manage the suppression register

Compliance › Suppression › Active Suppressions shows everyone currently blocked from receiving mail, and why (bounce, complaint, unsubscribe, manual). A wrongly-suppressed contact can be reinstated with a documented reason — it's never a silent delete.

3

Configure delivery & reputation thresholds

Compliance › Configuration › Delivery & Reputation sets the bounce-rate and complaint-rate warning/critical thresholds that trigger operator alerts — and, at the critical threshold, can auto-suspend a run.

05

Campaign Operator

Presses send on a frozen, cleared list — and can pull the plug if something looks wrong.

Group: Campaign Operator Only sees campaigns that already passed preflight
1

Find what's ready

Compliance › Execution › Ready to Send — every campaign that passed preflight and is waiting on you, and only you, to start it.

2

Start execution

Open the Campaign Run and click Start Execution. Sending is throttled and queued automatically — you don't need to watch it constantly.

3

Watch it land, or step in

Compliance › Execution › Active Runs and Completed Runs track every run in flight or finished. If bounce or complaint rates spike mid-send, an alert appears and — past the critical threshold — the run can auto-suspend on its own.

06

Operations Administrator

Everything the Campaign Operator can do, plus the delivery provider itself.

Group: Operations Administrator Superset of Campaign Operator
1

Send campaigns like an Operator

Everything in the Campaign Operator section above works identically for this role — Ready to Send, Start Execution, Active Runs, all of it.

2

Configure the delivery provider

This role additionally reaches Compliance › Configuration › Delivery & Reputation — the same screen shown in the Compliance Administrator section — to set provider credentials and sending thresholds, without needing full Compliance Administrator access to purposes and brands.

Why a separate role Keeping "who can send" and "who owns consent policy" separate means an operations engineer can tune delivery infrastructure without ever touching what counts as valid consent.
07

Privacy Officer

Handles the human side of privacy law: access, erasure, and how long data is kept.

Group: Privacy Officer Privacy requests + retention policy
1

Open the request

Compliance › Privacy › Privacy Requests lists every access, erasure, or correction request, whichever stage it's at.

2

Verify identity, then run discovery

Record how identity was confirmed, click Verify Identity, then Run Discovery to have the system find every record tied to that person — consent, suppression, send history, and more — before anything is decided.

3

Execute the request

Click Execute to carry out an access or erasure request. If a legal hold covers this person, execution is blocked automatically and logged — never silently skipped.

4

Set retention policy

Compliance › Privacy › Retention Policies defines how long each data category is kept. Preview Impact shows what a policy would affect before it ever runs for real.

08

Legal Hold Administrator

Freezes specific records — or the whole company — against retention and erasure.

Group: Legal Hold Administrator Overrides retention & erasure while active
1

Place a hold

Compliance › Privacy › Legal Holds › New. Set a reason and a scope — one recipient, or the entire company for a broader investigation.

2

It takes effect on save

Once saved, the hold is Active immediately — any matching retention or erasure action is blocked and recorded from this point on, with no extra step required.

3

Release it when the matter closes

Click Release Hold and give a closing reason. Retention and erasure resume normally for anything the hold was covering.

Don't forget this step A hold left active — especially a company-wide one — blocks retention and erasure for everyone until it's released. Release it as soon as the reason for it is gone.
09

Compliance Audit Reviewer

Read-only, everywhere — proof of what happened, not a way to change it.

Group: Compliance Audit Reviewer Cannot create, edit, or delete anything
1

Open a campaign archive

Every completed campaign leaves a locked archive record — Compliance › Audit › Campaign Archives — with the exact content, recipient counts, and approval trail as they were at send time, permanently.

Click Verify Integrity at any time to confirm the archive hasn't been tampered with since it was sealed.

2

Trace every retention & erasure action

Compliance › Privacy › Retention Action Ledger is the append-only record of every retention and erasure action ever taken — including ones a legal hold blocked.

3

Review the approval trail

Compliance › Campaigns › Approval History shows who approved, rejected, or ran preflight on every campaign, and exactly when.

Newsletter Compliance User Guide — every screenshot above was captured directly from the running system. Menu labels and button names match what you'll see exactly; if your screen looks different, check with your Compliance Administrator that you hold the right role for this section.
